focus_check: Water fund cells re-read on p7 and p2. p7 Water: charges for services 169,991; personnel 52,707 + operating 41,593 + supplies 5,825 = 100,125 (printed total ties); operating income printed 73,032 but 169,991 - 100,125 = 69,866 (short 3,166). Total column likewise: 278,528 - 195,358 = 83,170 vs printed 86,336. Sewer (62,236 - 47,329 = 14,907) and Sanitation (46,301 - 47,904 = -1,603) tie. Water's lower rows tie from the printed 73,032: 246 - 30,496 - 7,194 = -37,444; 73,032 - 37,444 = 35,588; 320,695 + 35,588 = 356,283. p2 adds up: Water expenditures 137,815 = 100,125 + 30,496 + 7,194; business-type general revenues 2,799 + 3,166 = 5,965; 45,480 + 5,965 = 51,445 = p7 increase. So the gap is in the report itself (p7 has no row for the 3,166 that its operating income includes), not a misread. It is correctly recorded in report_discrepancies, with the 3,166 receipt taken from p2.

issues.on_page: Township levy 9,192 (printed under Intergovernmental, Streets column)
issues.issue: A township levy comes from a local government, not the state. County/other local governments may fit better; state aid is defensible only because the page groups it under Intergovernmental.
Business-type cost-type line. Under the 2026-10-28/10-29 rules it could be category Operating rather than the function category utilities. This is a judgment call.

issues.on_page: Woodlawn Cemetery column (Personnel 447, Operating 2,922, Capital outlay 1,100)
issues.issue: The statement (p4) counts cemetery spending under Public Health and Safety (40,736 = Police 37,367 + Cemetery 3,369), and the receipts line uses public safety. The detail uses health/welfare (also detail[35], detail[36] function). This is defensible but inconsistent with the statement.
